---
title: Glossary
description: "One-line definitions of the terms used across these docs."
---

## The notation

| Term | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **Studyflow** | A notation for writing down a whole study --- what happens, in what order, to whom, and what data goes in and out --- so that people and software read the same description. See [Introduction](../index.qmd). |
| **a studyflow** | One study written in that notation: one diagram, one file. |
| **BPMN** | Business Process Model and Notation, the ISO/IEC 19510 standard for describing processes. Studyflow builds on it, so a studyflow opens in other BPMN tools. See [BPMN mapping](bpmn.qmd). |
| **`.studyflow.yaml`** | The file a studyflow lives in: plain text you can read, diff, and review. See [File format](file-format.qmd). |
| **Element set** | A group of elements that ship together. Four are always available; agentic, ml, and eeg are switched on when you need them. See [Elements](elements.qmd#the-seven-element-sets). |

## What you draw

| Term | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **Element** | Anything on the canvas: a step, an event, a gateway, a dataset. |
| **Activity** | A step in the study, drawn as a rounded box --- a task, a sub-process, or a call to another studyflow. |
| **Event** | A point where something happens, drawn as a circle: the participant enters, a timer fires, the study ends. |
| **Gateway** | A point where the path splits or rejoins, drawn as a diamond. |
| **Sequence flow** | A solid arrow: the participant, or the pipeline, goes this way next. |
| **Data association** | A dashed line between a step and a data element, saying what that step reads or writes. |
| **Pool** | A box around a whole participant group or agent, used when a study has more than one party in it. |
| **Choreography** | A way of drawing the exchange between two parties rather than one party's own path. |

## In a study

| Term | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **`Study`** | The diagram as a whole: the study, its authors, its version, and where it runs. |
| **`Actor`** | A pool of participants --- human, LLM, software agent, or instrument. |
| **Instrument** | The software that delivers a task, or the standard questionnaire a form implements. |
| **`CognitiveTask`** | A cognitive test the participant takes, delivered by an experiment package. |
| **`Questionnaire`** | A self-report form, standard or your own. |
| **`RandomGateway`** | Random assignment: each participant takes one of the outgoing arrows, one arm per arrow. |
| **`EligibilityGateway`** | A screening gate: eligible participants carry on, everyone else is screened out. |
| **`Dataset`** | A collection of data the study reads or produces, in a declared standard. |
| **`Parameters`** | A named group of settings connected into the steps that read them, so a study varies by editing values rather than the flow. |
| **Checklist** | Reporting items written on the step that records them, ticked off as the study progresses. |
| **Completion code** | The code a participant takes back to the recruitment platform when the study ends. |

## Reading and running

| Term | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **The modeler** | The web app where you draw and edit a studyflow. |
| **The browser runner** | The app that takes one participant through a study, screen by screen. |
| **The Python runner** | The program that executes an analysis or preprocessing studyflow on your machine. |
| **The CLI** | The `studyflow` command: convert, check, inspect, and run a file from a terminal. See [Command line and URLs](cli.qmd). |
| **Run** | One execution of a studyflow --- one participant's session, or one pass of a pipeline. |
| **Run repository** | The folder a run writes into --- outputs, log, and a stamped copy of the study --- and also a git repository. Its name is the run id, and without `git` installed a run leaves no step records. |
| **Seed** | The number the random draws start from. Pin it and the gateway draws repeat; leave it unset and each run records the one it drew. |
| **Provenance trail** | The record carried in the file of who changed it, what ran, when, and with which seed. See [Views and the record](../run/provenance.qmd). |
| **View** | One reading of the same file: the study itself, a schedule, a checklist, or the provenance record. See [Views and the record](../run/provenance.qmd). |
